reader.requirement: At --std 85, when the SD (file-name-1) contains only fixed length records (an explicit RECORD CONTAINS integer-1, or the implementor's implied fixed format), every record read from a USING file (file-name-2, of any organization: sequential, relative, indexed) that is shorter than that fixed length must be released to the sort space-filled on the right from the first position after its last character; a variable-length SD gets no fill (each record released at the size it was read).
reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect|IsAtLeast|Std' over SortEmitter.cs: no match; grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect' over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO: only connector, status and report-writer files, not CobolSort, RecordFill or SortKeyColumns; SortBinder's edition reads (RELEASE range at line 517, SAME RECORD AREA at line 927) are not on this path; FileModel.RecordSizeVaries / ImpliesVariableFormat read no edition (the implied RECORD clause is the edition-independent determination D-FRA).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (the national-space arm of ShortRecordFillNational is unreachable at 85, which has no national class; the alphanumeric space is the 1985 fill)

reader.notes: EmitInputFile releases each as-if READ record through CobolSort.FillTo(tmp, sdWidth, national) when the SD is fixed (SortVaryingOf null), which RecordFill.Fit pads with spaces; a varying SD releases FileCurrentRecord at the read length. Whether a file without a RECORD clause is fixed is implementor defined at 1985 (II.2.1.4.3); the compiler's D-FRA answer (fixed unless a record is variable-length) is applied uniformly.

refuter.evidence: su1.cob (runs/su1-005, --std 85): USING an ODO sequential file, a RECORD VARYING indexed file (records of 6 and 3) and a relative file with 01s of 6 and 2, into a fixed 6-char SD: [SZTUVW] [RSTUVW] [HMN   ] [GHIJKL] [5ABCDE] [2XYCDE] [1QYCDE]. The indexed 3-char record is space filled. The ODO and two-01 files have no RECORD clause; the compiler writes them as fixed 6-byte records (su1u.dat is 18 bytes, 5ABCDE2XYCDE1QYCDE), so they are read at 6 and no fill applies. That is the implementor choice §1985:II.2.1.4.3 leaves open ('OK  §1985:II.2.1.4.3 ... the text is in the clause'). su2.cob (runs/su2-001): an SD with RECORD CONTAINS 8 CHARACTERS and a 6-char 01 (legal by 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR1'), USING a 6-char file, GIVING a RECORD CONTAINS 10 file: su2g.dat holds 'AFIRST    BSECND    ', so the fill is to the SD's fixed length, not to its 01's size. cite.py 'OK  §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR1  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'.
